Feature overview

Android compatibility

Supports Android 7.0 through Android 17 and newer releases, with enhanced threading on Android 10 and newer. The HDR and cutout-free fullscreen mode provides the most immersive experience. Core pinning helps increase performance, and high-refresh-rate screen support keeps motion smooth. ARMv7 and ARMv8 builds are available, with full compatibility across Adreno, PowerVR and Mali GPUs.

Language support

Localization files load from the same paths as on PC. Advanced language features, such as morphological forms, grammatical cases and tense variations, work again, and localized voice audio is restored. Right-to-left languages like Arabic, Hebrew and Persian are supported, fonts included. Languages the original game never shipped with get context-aware, high-quality AI translations, and a built-in toolkit to translate into new languages. Diagnostic tools check language files for problems.

Installation

Localizations can be installed from the Library in the launcher, or by placing their files directly in the appropriate folders.

Folder paths

Localization files are read from these folders, where {code} is the language code, such as en or ar:

  • patch/languages/{code}/ for game text
  • patch/Modules/{module}/languages/{code}/ for module text
  • patch/Data/languages/{code}/font_data.xml for the font's glyph table
  • main/Textures/languages/{code}/font.dds for the font's texture atlas
  • patch/Modules/{module}/Sounds/languages/{code}/ for audio
  • main/Sounds/languages/{code}/ for audio

Controls customization

Control the game with on-screen touch controls, a gamepad, or a keyboard and mouse, and configure them from the launcher. Choose a theme for the touch controls, adjust sensitivity and inversion, and choose whether directional buttons respond to swipes or taps. Add custom keys and choose their icons. Touch controls appear conditionally for the current screen and react as the game changes screens, so the controls match what you are doing.

Game modules

Module directory routing works again, allowing you to play custom community-made modules, and assets load correctly, with fallbacks. Shader compatibility and transparency issues are fixed, along with material differences and animation problems. Control discovery suggests mapping buttons to the keys a module expects. Colors and icons can be customized for specific modules, and for engine mods bundled into modules.

Module Development
Touch UI customization

touch.csv changes how the touch buttons look and where they start. It is a plain text file with one setting per line. Here is a small example:

attack.color|red
defend.x|80
*.color|#FFD700

Read it line by line:

  • attack.color|red makes the attack button red.
  • defend.x|80 moves the defend button so its centre is 80% of the way across the screen, counted from the left.
  • *.color|#FFD700 makes every other button gold. The attack button stays red, because its own line overrides *.

Save the file as touch.csv in a language folder of your module:

  • patch/Modules/{module}/languages/en/touch.csv applies to every language. Put most settings here.
  • patch/Modules/{module}/languages/{code}/touch.csv applies only when the game uses that language, for example a different icon with a letter in it.

Keys from the game language's file override the same keys from the English file.

Each line has two parts, split at the first | character (the vertical bar):

  • Left of the bar: the button name, a dot, and the setting name. defend.x means "the x position of the defend button".
  • Right of the bar: the value, such as 80, red or #FFD700.
  • One setting per line, saved as UTF-8 text. A line with no | is skipped.
  • If the same setting appears twice in one file, the later line wins.
  • * in place of the button name means every button. It works only for color and background, not for position, size, icon or shown.
Button names
  • Battle: attack, defend, kick, jump, use, zoom, switch_weapon, next_shield, crouch, weapon_mode, drop, camera, leave, menu, chat, orders, orders_more
  • Orders: orders_up, orders_choose, orders_down, orders_back
  • Map: map_look, fast_travel, map_camera, stop_rest, map_menu
  • Trade: trade_take_all, trade_give_all, trade_cancel
  • Party: party_stack, party_ten
  • Other: screen_back, dialog_up, dialog_select, dialog_down
  • Assignable: extra1 to extra10
  • Mod: mod.{mod id}.{button id}

The movement stick is not a touch.csv button. Its size and position are chosen by the player, so touch.csv cannot change it.

The settings:

  • attack.icon|M4 20 L20 4 M14 4 H20 V10 sets the icon as SVG path commands (M, L, H, V, C, S, Q, Z) on a 24 by 24 grid. To change one version of a button only, add its action: kick.game.kick.icon is the kick on foot, and kick.game.action.icon is the kick while riding.
  • *.color|#FFD700 sets the colour of the icon or label. Write #RRGGBB, #AARRGGBB, or a colour name such as red.
  • defend.background|#C0301010 sets the disc behind the button while it is not pressed.
  • defend.x|80 and defend.y|89 set the centre of the button, as a percent of the screen width and height, from 0 to 100.
  • defend.size|14 sets the diameter, as a percent of the screen's shorter side, from 6 to 40.
  • kick.shown|false sets whether the button is on screen by default. Write true or false.

Values outside their range are limited to it, and a bad colour or bad key is ignored. Positions are only defaults: a button the player moved, resized or hid keeps the player's setting. Reset in the editor brings back the module's values.

Engine mods path and packaging

A module can ship engine mods in patch/Modules/{module}/mods/. Each entry is either:

  • a .zip of the package, with its files at the root or in one folder
  • a folder with the package files: manifest.json, mod.armv7.o and/or mod.arm64.o, and optionally mod.jar

When the player selects the module, they are asked once whether to run them. They run with that module only, with their default settings.

Multiplayer and Engine upgrade

Play on multiplayer servers compatible with versions 1.158 and 1.174, including over LAN. Browse and join custom servers, and the launcher automatically switches to the module required by the selected server.

PC engine features and script opcodes are updated through Warband 1.173. Character import and export are supported. Multiplayer works with Warband 1.174.

Gameplay additions

Live Sky shaders animate the clouds and add moving effects to the night sky. Live Trees shaders make trees and other foliage sway. Fire Damage and Water Physics & Drowning are available from the Library: fire can hurt characters, and water adds wading, sinking and drowning. Hit Vibration can make the phone vibrate when you take or deal damage, with stronger hits producing stronger vibrations. All these features can be enabled or disabled in the launcher.

Improved loading speed and gameplay performance

The game starts faster by reading files at the same time and loading module data and textures in small batches. It also compiles shaders on several threads and caches them, so they load faster next time. Texture streaming keeps textures small until they appear on screen, then makes them smaller again when they are no longer needed. This saves memory.

The ARM64 game was freshly retranslated with new optimizations, and slow engine areas were rewritten. As a result, the ARM64 build now outperforms the original ARMv7 build. The rewritten areas include animation, visibility, collisions, terrain, targeting and drawing, reducing the work these tasks take. The game and graphics can also use the device's fastest CPU cores, while background tasks use the others. The world map stays smoother when you speed up time.

Texture formats

Devices that already support the DXT BC1–3 texture formats use native textures right away. Devices without DXT support get a choice: convert textures once and load them quickly, or transcode them on every load. The retexcon library module, written from scratch, handles ASTC, ETC1, ETC2 and RGB8 formats, including transparency. It reaches 99.8% accuracy and runs many times faster than the open source library from ARM. For low-end devices, block size and texture resolution can be configured, with exceptions for important textures such as fonts and skyboxes. The 64-bit build loads textures into separate memory regions, which allows larger textures and leaves more room for the game's other resources. HDR skybox textures are fully supported. Support for TexturesHD is restored, and some textures were healed from DXT compression artefacts. Our texture engine also supports on-demand texture streaming, cutting the required RAM in half.

Post-processing and HDR

PostFX Restore brings back the post-processing pipeline missing from the mobile port: its render passes, shader techniques and effects such as exposure, bloom and blur. It uses higher-precision floating-point render targets when the device supports them. The game's gamma setting also works.

For supported devices and screens, HDR output uses HDR10 or HLG to extend the brightness and color range beyond standard output. Advanced per-pixel tone mapping lets bright areas reach HDR highlights while preserving the rest of the image. Automatic mode prefers HLG and then HDR10. HDR output requires support from the device, graphics driver and display; otherwise the game uses standard SDR output.

Flickering reduction

The game can use a 24-bit depth buffer instead of its original 16-bit one. This helps stop distant surfaces from flickering. The Scene depth setting offers 24-bit (D24S8) and, on supported devices, 32-bit float (D32F).

Framebuffer Format controls how much colour detail the screen can show. It offers the formats supported by the device: RGB888 (24-bit), RGB10A2 (30-bit) and RGBA16F (64-bit float). Higher colour detail helps reduce visible bands in gradients. GPU dithering can also be turned off; it can cause a fixed dot pattern on 16-bit colour.

The custom-made TAA mod adds temporal anti-aliasing, which the original game did not have. Like modern graphics features such as NVIDIA DLSS, it uses information from nearby frames to smooth jagged edges and reduce flicker.

Tree detail levels blend smoothly as you move, including for trees placed in the world. This avoids sudden changes, flicker, moving lines and overlapping trunks as trees switch detail levels. Leaves keep their shape while fading, without dark edges. Grass and small plants fade into view instead of appearing all at once.

Improved shadows

Environment shadows are restored on non-Tegra graphics chips, with smoother edges instead of square blocks. Fixes help keep shadows from disappearing after graphics resources reset or if the shadow map fails. Nearby character shadows update more often and are more accurate. Character and tree shadows no longer pop into view; their transitions are smooth. The optional depth-texture mode brings soft-edged environment shadows and a closer fit for sharper detail.

Scene transitions

Scene changes can fade out and back in to hide black flashes and leftover parts of the previous scene. The previous image stays visible while the new scene is being drawn. Fades can be turned off.

TTS and STT

Text-to-speech can read conversations and your chosen dialogue options aloud. Speech is available in supported languages. You can also enable spoken notifications, scene messages and multiplayer chat.

Speech-to-text lets you dictate chat with the phone's speech recognition. In battle, use the microphone button or a mapped key to speak orders: command named groups or everyone, or run one of your custom orders. The speech features can be configured in the launcher's mod settings.

Debug overlays

Show FPS, RAM usage, ping, device temperature and thermal throttling status in an overlay. Adjust gamma, saturation and contrast to tune the game's image.

UI customization

Adjust message size, set the interface to 4:3 or 16:9, and control whether touch buttons stay inside the game picture. You can keep battles and the world map full-screen, hide pop-ups, and hide on-screen error messages.

The launcher includes an editor for the game's rgl_config.txt settings. Search settings, edit them with sliders, switches and menus, or use a raw text view. Compare values with the game defaults and reset the configuration when needed. Changes take effect the next time the game reads the file.

Savegame management

Manage saved games from the launcher: import and export save files, create and restore backups, and edit savedata.

M&BTool is an unofficial fan project, made by fans for fans.
